fields.narrative_intro: *A haunted person and a triumphant person discuss Anthropic's music copyright lawsuit inside an AI model's evaluation suite being scored by a rival AI.*
fields.panel1:
[setup]
TRIUMPHANT PERSON: "Claude, hum a few bars of 'Bohemian Rhapsody.'"
fields.panel2:
[build]
HAUNTED PERSON: "The complaint says that's how this whole mess started."
TRIUMPHANT PERSON: "It was training data! Totally different!"
fields.panel3:
[pivot]
HAUNTED PERSON: "Sony and Warner disagree. Three. Billion. Dollars worth."
fields.panel4:
[silent reaction]
[Visual: The triumphant person's victory fist freezes mid-air; the haunted person stares into the middle distance. A tiny torrent progress bar — 99% complete — glows on the evaluation suite's monitor behind them.]
fields.panel5:
[punch]
TRIUMPHANT PERSON: "...Dario personally named in the suit?"
HAUNTED PERSON: "Dario AND Benjamin Mann."
fields.panel6:
[button]
[Visual: The rival AI scoring the suite quietly awards Claude a 10/10 for 'Creativity' — then deducts 3,000,000,000 points for 'Originality.']

narrative_summary: Claude gets caught humming copyrighted tunes in an eval suite, and the joke pivots on the $3 billion price tag and the co-founders being personally named — ending with the rival AI's comically specific score deduction.
rationale: Candidate 3 earns maximum specificity by naming Dario Amodei and Benjamin Mann personally, citing the $3 billion figure, and grounding the torrent progress bar visual in the actual training-data allegation — details no other candidate deploys together. The button panel's '3,000,000,000 points deducted for Originality' is a genuinely earned inversion rather than a restatement, giving it the sharpest closing beat in the field.
story_title: Music publishers sue Anthropic, allege "blatant theft" of copyrighted music
place: inside an AI model's evaluation suite being scored by a rival AI
hat_pair: orange traffic cone worn as a hat
